changelog_from_0_1: Law is a 3-axis object plus shape: (quantity, transition, precondition, schema). The kappa pair forced this: same quantity, same transition, same schema — the precondition alone flips FALSIFIED to PROVED.

Warrant gains SUPPORT (the measurement carrier) and world_revision. Two invalidation modes: support intact (quantity moves under known laws) vs support changed (re-derive, all bets off).
Instrument model is many-to-many: an instrument is a BUNDLE of claims on law cells, each with entitlement, settlement rule, and witness. 'A currency is a claim on a law' stays as the page copy.
Cells carry a counterlaw pointer: every proved conditional law names its falsified unrestricted sibling. The pair teaches more than either member.

Status vocabulary: PROVED, PROPERTY-TESTED, MODEL-CHECKED-FRAGMENT, EMPIRICAL, OPEN, NOT_APPLICABLE, FALSIFIED. Falsified-by-design rows must keep failing: a passing red row means the definition changed.

changelog_from_0_2: TWO STRATA. Object laws constrain quantities inside a domain (the eight). Meta-laws constrain relationships between layers/compositions: EQUIVARIANCE (new, promoted on evidence), CLOSURE, COHERENCE, REFINEMENT, WELL_FOUNDEDNESS, PROGRESS/LIVENESS (candidate). CLOSURE/COHERENCE/WELL_FOUNDEDNESS moved from candidate-orbitals to the meta stratum — they were never awkward ninth orbitals; they live one level up.

EQUIVARIANCE earned its place by catching two real bugs in one review round: scalar kappa is not renaming-invariant at SCC ties (360/360 split over 720 relabelings of one graph — verified), and the kernel's v1 state digest collapsed binder connectivity (different programs digested identically — verified against the shipped code, fixed, regression L-EQV-1 added).

KAPPA IS NOW A PROFILE. kappa_S is defined per SCC support; topology emits {(support, size, kappa_S, cut witness)}; POLICY selects (largest / max-kappa / threshold / query-overlap); the warrant records both. The clean theorem C2-prime: for fixed SCC support S, adding an edge inside G[S] never decreases kappa_S — exhaustive n=4 (9,240 internal additions, 0 decreases) + argument. Slogan: Measurement is invariant. Selection is policy. Warrant authorizes.

WARRANT v3: freshness binds to what the derivation READ, not to a global epoch — {exact: [resource@version], predicates: [scope-query@version]}. The predicate scope handles the phantom-read problem kappa exposed (new edges from a node that did not exist when you read can grow the SCC without touching any old edge). Independently mirrored by Atomix's read-scope sealing.

EXECUTION PRIVILEGES. The operational meaning of an established law: a freedom the runtime may exercise. Confluence -> reorder/parallelize reduction; monotonicity/I-confluence -> coordination-free merge; locality -> concurrent disjoint transitions; idempotence -> retry/dedupe; conservation -> bounded transfer accounting; binding -> context-checked consumption; decay -> deterministic expiry; annihilation -> fail-closed refusal; derivation -> independent regeneration; equivariance -> placement/renaming freedom (node ids and worker placement cannot leak into semantics). A FALSIFIED law is executable too: it REMOVES an optimizer permission (unrestricted kappa-monotonicity is forbidden as a rewrite justification).

NAMING SPLIT adopted: STATE_APPLY (period COMMIT), ARTIFACT_COMMIT (//commit canonicalize-freeze), EFFECT_SETTLE (external finality). Three different irreversibility boundaries deserve three names in IR and films.

FOUR PLANES for TRVM: INTERACT (core rules, confluence) / COLLAPSE-OBSERVE (readback; DUP-VAR & DUP-APP live here per upstream IC's Collapsing extension and forge/random_order.py's pre-existing guard) / WORLD (ADMIT-APPLY, CALM & I-confluence, walls) / EFFECT (seal -> revalidate -> settle). Walls = where the proof of coordination-free admissibility ends.

FRAMING. Cells are metamorphic relations (Q, T, P, R); the table is a domain-specific periodic grammar for DISCOVERING metamorphic relations and compiling the held ones into runtime privileges and the falsified ones into removed permissions.

HONESTY EDITS. L-MONO-1 renamed substitution-store inflationarity (a monotone-state ingredient; the CALM-level claim about specification outcomes belongs to the world layer — cf. Complete CALM, arXiv 2602.09435, verified). L-DERIV-4 reclassified as a DOMAIN-EXCLUSION witness (affinity is definitional; the witness shows why the domain boundary exists). Kernel's scheduler gate credited to forge/random_order.py, which already enforced it.

entries.statement: A warrant is a VERIFYING TRACE generalized: freshness(warrant, world) iff every exact read [resource@version] and every predicate scope [query@digest] re-evaluates unchanged. Unrelated writes never invalidate — freshness reads the footprint, not the world's write counter. (The build-systems verifying-trace idea, plus the predicate-lock idea from serializable databases, as one shape.)
entries.evidence: trvm_world.mjs L-WAR-1: component-size warrant fresh at seal and STILL fresh after 50 unrelated writes; goes stale precisely when its footprint moves (L-WAR-4).

entries.statement: The read footprint is an AUTHORITY CLAIM, so replay is JAILED: the derivation re-runs under a view that permits only the declared footprint — an undeclared read or scope refuses (undeclared-read, undeclared-scope), versions must match (footprint-version-mismatch), scopes must re-digest (scope-digest-mismatch), and value/witness/commitment re-derive (value-mismatch, witness-mismatch, warrant-id-mismatch, support-not-subset). A pruned footprint dies at the jail even when honestly resealed. Authority must not outrun evidence — the rounds-5/6 law, applied to reads.
entries.evidence: trvm_world.mjs L-WAR-2: honest replay ok; pruned-footprint, inflated-value, unsealed-mutation, and support-beyond-footprint forgeries each refused on their declared reason.

entries.statement: Exact reads alone cannot witness membership of a set that grew: a resource absent at read time can join the measured structure without touching any read resource (the kappa phantom case, executable). The guard is a predicate scope: a reified query whose digest is committed in the footprint; the phantom flips the digest and classifies scope_dirty even though every exact read is byte-identical. The UNGUARDED warrant's fresh-while-wrong witness is kept red by construction.
entries.evidence: trvm_world.mjs L-WAR-3: phantom constructed (new node + edge via a writer that leaves every read resource untouched): true size 3 vs warranted 2 with the naked warrant 'fresh'; the scope-guarded warrant classifies scope_dirty on the incident-edge digest.

entries.statement: Staleness is classified, each verdict with a complete witness (law:film.terminal-witness@1 applied to verdicts): support_changed (a support resource moved — re-derive), scope_dirty (a predicate scope moved — re-derive; the phantom lives here), support_intact (a read-but-not-support resource moved — eligible for EARLY CUTOFF: jailed re-derivation that reproduces the value refreshes the footprint and reseals instead of discarding).
entries.evidence: trvm_world.mjs L-WAR-4: three worlds, one verdict each, witnesses asserted; the support_intact case refreshes — value preserved, footprint reversioned, warrant_id resealed, refreshed warrant fresh.

entries.statement: Warrants and certificates speak ONE evidence language: a Footprint {exact, predicates} with footprint_id. The SchedulerCertificate maps into it — corpus{id,sha256} is one exact read, evidence is the value, the run-manifest hash is the witness — so certificate freshness IS warrant freshness. (The requirement round 5 adopted, discharged.)
entries.evidence: trvm_world.mjs L-WAR-5: the shipped 144-receipt certificate wrapped as a Warrant v3; fresh at seal, fresh under unrelated writes, support_changed exactly when the corpus resource moves.

entries.statement: A warrant cites another warrant ONLY through its publication — a world resource carrying {value, warrant_id, footprint_id} — and every publication read in a composite footprint is PAIRED with a reified freshness scope (warrant-fresh:<name>, the citee's footprint re-evaluated against the current world). Publication reads alone LAUNDER STALENESS: the citee can go phantom-stale without its publication moving, and the naive composite stays fresh while transitively wrong — that witness is constructed and kept red. The jail is the abstraction boundary: composite replay reads publications and freshness scopes, never citee internals.
entries.evidence: trvm_world.mjs L-COMP-1 (the composition phantom: citee scope_dirty and provably wrong, naive composite 'fresh', guarded composite scope_dirty on the same world); L-COMP-2 (chain + diamond: one ground movement dirties every guarded citer along both paths, with footprint dedup at the join); L-COMP-3 (honest composite replay ok; a replayer reaching for citee internals refuses undeclared-read; the pruned publication refuses undeclared-read).

entries.statement: The frame rule at the world layer (sigma T4's instance): a write's effect on a warrant's verdict is exactly predicted by footprint membership and scope influence. Writes outside a warrant's evidence (neither an exact-read resource nor influencing any scope result) can NEVER change its verdict; writes inside change it as classified (support hit -> support_changed; scope influence -> scope_dirty; non-support exact hit -> support_intact).
entries.evidence: trvm_world.mjs L-FRAME-1: 120/120 random writes (23 inside the evidence, 97 outside) with the predicted verdict matching the actual freshness classification on every draw.

entries.statement: World state is WRITE-MEDIATED: a resource's observable value cannot change except through a version-advancing World transition — same version IMPLIES same canonical value; every observable world mutation induces an observable world identity transition. Mechanism: a canonical resource-value domain (null, boolean, finite number, string, arrays, plain objects with sorted keys; everything else refuses world-value-not-canonical), the store owning canonical BYTES under TRVM-VALUE-v1 content hashes, and fresh parses on every read — both alias directions (ingress after put, egress through read results) die at the boundary. Deletions are TOMBSTONES: the deletion version is observable, so 'deleted' and 'never existed' do not collapse at the version layer.
entries.evidence: Round-8B audit witness AUDIT-WORLD-ALIAS, reproduced executably against v0.2.0: world.read(r).value.push(2) mutated the world with no put, no version change — freshness said fresh while jailed replay said value-mismatch (the two verifiers disagreed); the ingress variant leaked {a:{b:[1,99]}}. v0.3.0: L-ALIAS-1 (the witness verbatim now a no-op with verifier agreement restored; ingress and nested aliases dead; 6/6 non-canonical refusals); L-WORLD-1 (tombstone lifecycle, version=>hash).

entries.statement: FRESH implies REPLAY-COHERENT: for a deterministic derivation, if freshness(warrant, world) is fresh then jailed replay must succeed — the two verification mechanisms may not disagree. This is the corollary of write-mediation that warrant soundness actually consumes; the audit witness falsified exactly this implication on the aliasing substrate.

entries.statement: Support is DERIVED, not declared into authority: replay(D, W) = ok implies support(D) == support(W) exactly — the subset rule (support ⊆ exact footprint) is necessary but NOT sufficient, and both replayers enforce both properties (support-mismatch, the tenth refusal). Support is CANONICAL at seal (sorted, deduplicated; reordering is a no-op by construction). refreshWarrant RESTORES derivation-produced support — a forged support cannot survive the early-cutoff path. Division of verification for the shipped receipt: grid_check holds the engine-free half (subset, canonical form, commitments); `trvm_world.mjs --check-receipt` rebuilds the world from the receipt's COMMITTED world_spec and replays both warrants — the engine half a tampered-but-resealed support cannot survive.

entries.statement: A maintenance pass visits every maintained warrant EXACTLY ONCE in a deterministic dependency order (Kahn, sorted ready-set): no citer is classified or refreshed before its citees are current, diamonds re-derive the shared citee once (not once per path), and a completed pass leaves every non-quarantined publication FRESH. Classification drives action: fresh -> replay-validate (no-op); support_intact -> refresh (escalating to re-derive on value divergence); support_changed / scope_dirty -> re-derive.
entries.evidence: trvm_world.mjs L-MAINT-1 (chain A<-B<-C: order asserted from the receipt, convergence to all-fresh, values correct, B's new footprint cites A's NEW publication; the wrong-order counterfactual — C re-derived before A — carries the wrong value AND is detectably non-fresh, kept red); L-MAINT-4 (diamond: exactly 4 steps, join after both arms, identical pass_ids across identical runs).

entries.statement: Forged input is QUARANTINED, never repaired or propagated: external warrants replay-gate at register(); inside a pass, FRESH nodes are replay-validated (footprint versions permit replay exactly then) and a refusal quarantines the node — publication untouched, ids unchanged in the step record. Refresh/re-derive paths replace state with derivation truth and the receipt records both ids, so nothing forged ever ships as-is.
entries.evidence: trvm_world.mjs L-MAINT-3: the support-forged warrant refused at the register() door (support-mismatch) AND quarantined when poisoned directly into maintainer state — publication version unmoved.

entries.statement: The pass runs on a WORLD FORK; the real world is touched only by the atomic APPLY of the staged publication sequence after every node succeeded. A mid-pass failure discards the fork: publications, vclock, and maintainer state are byte-identical to before, and the receipt records {aborted, at} with completed steps for forensics.
entries.evidence: trvm_world.mjs L-MAINT-6: A re-derives on the fork, then B's measure throws — real world and state untouched. Enabled by the round-9 refactor: scope queries read through an interface, never a captured world reference, so World.fork() is total. Round-9B audit FALSIFIED the unconditional reading: a measureFn that retained the authoritative World wrote it mid-pass and threw — the 'aborted' pass left vclock 3->4 and a leaked resource, and the receipt sampled the vclock in the catch handler, reporting vclock_before=4 (the escaped transition normalized into the alleged pre-state). ATOMIC=false, RECEIPT-TRUTH=false, reproduced and frozen in probe_forkescape_v05_repro.mjs. The statement is made UNCONDITIONAL by law:maintenance.capability-confinement@1 (the world lock) plus the entry-clock capture; L-CONFINE-1 locks the witness. Round 9.3 (self-audit, provisional pending the external round-9D text, which arrived empty): the APPLY path itself sat after the abort-catch, so a mid-apply fault would leave the real world half-applied (append-only cannot roll back), skip sealReceipt, and propagate raw — the tear invisible to the record. Closed: staged publications are PRE-VALIDATED (canonicalized) before the first real write, making organic tears unreachable, and injected tears (documented fault port pass({faultApplyAfter})) are RECEIPTED truthfully — {aborted, torn, at: apply, applied: [prefix]}, vclock_after and the after-map reflecting the REAL half-applied world — with the next pass proven to repair and converge (L-APPLY-1). Also locked there: prototype-chain children of the sealed World carry no authority (private-field access throws), and constructor laundering yields only fresh isolated worlds.

entries.statement: The MaintenanceReceipt PROVES the pass rather than narrating it: the BEFORE and AFTER publication maps and the ordered steps are committed (pass_id = H('TRVM-MAINTPASS-v1' | vclocks | before | after | steps)), and AFTER must be reconstructible from BEFORE + steps by arithmetic — none/quarantined steps preserve ids and versions, refreshed/rederived steps advance the publication version and change the warrant_id. A converged pass is a receipted NO-OP: all-none steps, vclock unmoved, before == after.
entries.evidence: trvm_world.mjs L-MAINT-2 (the no-op pass proven, not asserted); grid_check v2.9 recomputes the commitment and performs the full before+steps=after reconstruction engine-free on the shipped maintenance_receipt.json; the maintenance receipt is deterministic across identical runs.

entries.statement: The warrant DAG is PROVED acyclic, not assumed: the construction API cannot express a forward reference (cites must already exist), and every pass independently re-verifies via Kahn leftover against direct defs poisoning — a cycle refuses the WHOLE pass, names its members, and leaves the world untouched.

entries.statement: Code executing within a maintenance pass cannot MUTATE the authoritative World except through capabilities explicitly supplied by the transaction: for the duration of a pass the root World is LOCKED — put/del/registerQuery refuse world-write-during-maintenance — the fork stays writable, and only the pass's commit CAPABILITY (a per-lock key) may apply staged writes; finally-semantics release the lock on success, exception, quarantine, and cycle refusal alike. Escaped writes become aborts, never corruption. Independently: the pass-entry vclock is captured BEFORE any adversarial code runs, so aborted receipts report the ACTUAL entry clock. Fork-and-apply is thereby an isolation boundary, not a convention. Scope: PASSES — register/addGround derive on the live world by design and their writes are ordinary mediated transitions; execution in a separate authority domain (worker isolation) is the declared v-next for portable/ic32 derivations.
entries.evidence: Round-9B witness AUDIT-FORK-ESCAPE reproduced against v0.5.0 (ATOMIC=false; receipt vclock_before reported the already-mutated clock) and frozen. v0.6.0: L-CONFINE-1 (the witness verbatim: the escaped write REFUSES, the pass aborts tagged at its node, world byte-untouched, receipt reports the entry clock, lock released); L-CONFINE-2 (composite del-escape, armed poisoned-query escape, refresh-path escape each abort with the world untouched; a fresh-validation escape is converted to QUARANTINE; the lock survives cycle refusal; forged commit / double lock / wrong-key unlock each refuse). All twenty prior batteries re-ran green under the lock. Round-9C audit follow-up FALSIFIED the implementation again, exactly where the audit predicted: the lock key was a PUBLIC property (world._lockKey), so a retained closure stole it and committed THROUGH the lock — the witness leaked mid-pass without even aborting (vclock 3->5) — and, key or no key, res/log/queries/vclock were public fields open to raw mutation bypassing every guard (world.res.set landed a ghost resource silently). Both reproduced and frozen in probe_keytheft_v06_repro.mjs. v0.7.0 closes structurally: all state in true private fields (#res/#vclock/#log/#queries/#lockKey), crypto-random key (randomBytes), read surface via copying getters, World.prototype and every instance FROZEN (patching throws). L-CONFINE-3 locks the theft witness and the sealed-internals matrix. Stated residual unchanged: same-realm JS is option 1's outer limit; worker-domain isolation remains the declared v-next.

entries.statement: The canonical digest is DEFINED as sha256 of a canonical signature string, and those pre-hash BYTES are a published artifact rather than an internal detail: stateDigest(s) == sha256(stateSignature(s)) through one code path, never two, so a shipped signature cannot drift from the digest it explains. golden_prehash_vectors.json carries the signature strings for every corpus state (initial and normal form) plus the §5 compaction boundary, so a second implementation diffs the STRING and sees where its canonical form diverges instead of only learning that a hash differs.
entries.evidence: Kernel row L-BYTES-1: 48/48 corpus states satisfy sha256(stateSignature) == semStateId, the compaction boundary is well-formed on all of them (7 compacted to exactly 65 chars, longest uncompacted exactly 80), and equivariance is asserted at the BYTE level — alpha-variants and label permutations produce the identical signature string, which a digest-level check could not distinguish from a canonical form that agrees only after hashing. grid_check v2.13 verifies the shipped vectors engine-free: every signature is re-hashed against its id, every normal-form nf_id is matched against the refinement receipt, and the compaction row's reconstructed pre-compaction string is re-hashed against the emitted compacted signature. Negative battery cases prehash-signature-tampered, prehash-id-resealed, prehash-nfid-unanchored, and prehash-compaction-lie each die on a distinct diagnostic.

entries.statement: The object HOLDING the maintenance lock is itself an authority surface and must be confined like the one it locks. The Maintainer's root reference and methods are not reassignable (instance and prototype frozen, setPrototypeOf refused), and registration is refused re-entrantly for the duration of a pass. Its defs/state maps stay mutable BY DESIGN: the external-ingest position already exists and is modelled by register(); the attack closed here is not that a map can be written but that it could be written from inside a transaction.
entries.evidence: World row L-COORD-1 (4/4): a derivation calling addGround mid-pass is refused with maintainer-reentrancy-refused and leaves no def and no after-map entry; assigning this.world is refused by the instance freeze so the pass ABORTS with a receipt instead of unlocking the wrong world and bricking the authoritative one; instance and prototype sealer overrides and setPrototypeOf all throw, and the pass seals a real 64-char pass_id; a nested pass refuses. The pre-fix witnesses are frozen RED in probe_maintainer_9d_repro.mjs against World 0.7.1, where three of the audit's four reproduced. grid_check v2.14 scans for the guard constructs; negative cases coordinator-freeze-stripped, coordinator-proto-freeze-stripped and coordinator-reentrancy-stripped die on distinct diagnostics.

entries.statement: Once a maintenance pass begins, every semantic input governing it — definitions, derivation bindings, dependency topology and coordinator state — is immutable for the duration of the transaction, and no RETAINED ALIAS may mutate those inputs outside the coordinator's guarded transition API. Sealing the coordinator's properties is insufficient: a frozen property still points at a mutable Map, and a registration that stores the caller's spec by reference leaves authoritative configuration in the caller's hands. Writes go through stores that consult the in-flight flag, values are owned and frozen on the way in, and the pass computes against a definition view captured at entry. Separately, a receipt may not assemble one apparently authoritative fact out of two independent sources: publication fields come from the publication, coordinator state is compared against it, and disagreement is DECLARED.
entries.evidence: World row L-COORD-2 (4/4): an in-pass defs.set refuses and leaves no GHOST in defs or in the after-map; an in-pass cross-node state.set refuses and the receipt's warrant_id now comes from the publication and equals the world's; a caller-owned spec retained across registration is severed and the pass derives honestly with the stored spec frozen against assignment; and poisoning from OUTSIDE a pass still works — the seam L-MAINT-3/L-MAINT-5 depend on — with the snapshot reporting coordinator_diverged rather than preferring a side. All three attack witnesses are frozen RED against World 0.8.0 in probe_coordinator_alias_9d1_repro.mjs, where they reproduced 0/3 confined. grid_check v2.15 scans for the guard constructs; three negative cases die on distinct diagnostics.

entries.statement: Ownership on ingest must be TRANSITIVE and SCHEMA-COMPLETE. Transitive: freezing a record while leaving its nested value/witness objects shared leaves an in-pass write that no store guard observes, because no set() occurs. Schema-complete: an ownership layer may sever references, it may NOT silently drop fields — dropping inputs/law_refs/naive turned alias-severing into an undeclared semantic projection over derivation_id. Owned values pass through canonicalBytes, the boundary the World already trusts, rather than a second clone algorithm; unknown spec fields are refused rather than discarded. And divergence detection may not be identity-only: a coordinator record mutated without resealing keeps a matching warrant_id, so the published VALUE is compared too.
entries.evidence: World row L-COORD-2 (4/4) plus probe_realm_9d2_repro.mjs, where both defects reproduced against World 0.9.0 — `m.state.get("B").value.x = 999` succeeded with isFrozen(value)=false and coordinator_diverged absent because the ids still matched, and a spec carrying inputs/law_refs/naive stored only [measure,predicate,measureFn] and derived a warrant with law_refs []. Both are CONFINED at 0.10.0 with the witness frozen red at 0.9.0.

entries.statement: An audit result is creditable only if the instrument independently proves that the intended perturbation occurred, the intended execution path was exercised, and the measured predicate is the one reported. A falsifier that forges nothing, runs nothing, or measures a different predicate than it names is VACUOUS, and a vacuous falsifier is worse than an absent one because the roster still counts it. Mutation cases must show before_hash != after_hash before the detector's verdict counts.
entries.evidence: negative_battery.sh computes a pre- and post-perturbation digest of every scratch tree and refuses to credit a case whose forgery changed nothing (diagnostic: VACUOUS). This law is retrospective as much as prospective: it covers the unset $SCRATCH that meant a case could never execute, the hand-typed 44/44 that stopped counting the cases, the hard-coded "1.0.2" replacement that a version bump would have turned into a no-op, the prototype half of the authority graph that went untested, the false '9D-4 confined' produced by poisoning a node whose semantic path the pass overwrote, and a probe line that printed 'directly assignable' while testing typeof === 'function'. Six apparatus failures across four rounds, every one of which this rule would have caught mechanically. MECHANISED (both runners, v1.14.0): clause 1 — the intended target is DERIVED from the perturbation script (files opened for writing, files removed) and must EQUAL the set that actually changed, so a case editing the wrong artifact, or an extra one, fails as loudly as one editing nothing; clauses 2-3 — per-file digests before and after, refusing VACUOUS and naming the artifact perturbed; clause 5 — the specific diagnostic must match; clause 6 — CAUGHT increments only after all of the above. Both detectors were verified to FIRE by deliberately breaking a case (VACUOUS: 57/58; TARGET MISMATCH: 63/64) and restoring it. STILL DECLARED OPEN: clause 4, independent evidence that the intended EXECUTION PATH ran — the diagnostic match is a weak proxy, and the false '9D-4 confined' result came from a witness that never entered the semantic path it was written for. Closing it needs the verifier to report which rules it evaluated, not merely which one failed.

entries.statement: The apparatus is measured by a gate, not by attention. law:evidence.instrument-nonvacuity@1 requires each falsifier to be non-vacuous; this requires the HARNESS ITSELF to demonstrate that it detects the failure species that have actually occurred in this tree. Nine are enumerated and each has a meta-falsifier: working-directory dependence, an absent declared artifact, a present undeclared artifact, a perturbation that changes nothing, a case that DELETES rather than modifies, a case that moves an artifact it did not declare, a case whose expected diagnostic is not the one produced, a paired probe whose frozen side has been silently repaired, and — the one a battery of forgeries cannot see — an UNPERTURBED case tree that does not pass the checker. Eight require the harness to SAY SO; the ninth requires it to say nothing when nothing is wrong. Deliberately BOUNDED: this encodes the known failure species and does not recurse into tests of tests.
entries.evidence: harness_selftest.sh, 9/9. The motivating record is six consecutive rounds in which the instrument rather than the engine was wrong: the unset $SCRATCH, the hand-typed 44/44, the hard-coded "1.0.2" version forgery, the probe line printing 'directly assignable' while testing typeof, the false '9D-4 confined' from a witness that never entered its path, a non-vacuity law registered one round before its harness implemented it, a one-sided diff that called a deleting case vacuous, round 15's two CWD-relative reads — one of which scanned the empty string and reported success — and round 17's contaminated baseline, where every negative case since round 14 had run against a checker already reporting four unrelated failures. The self-test caught three defects in its own first draft: a header split that captured the run_case DEFINITION rather than its first invocation, an M-8 repair that did not neutralise the witness it was meant to neutralise, and an M-1 that asserted a PASSING verdict where its subject was an IDENTICAL one.

entries.statement: A perturbation-based result is admissible only if the IDENTICAL verifier, fixture, environment and artifact set satisfy their DECLARED baseline before the perturbation is applied. The word is DECLARED, not silent: each falsifier family names what its own clean state looks like. The negative battery's baseline is grid_check exiting 0 on the unperturbed fixture; the C bridge's is 48/48 byte equality; the kernel's is the canonical certificate and gates matching; a World attack probe's is the honest fixture satisfying the World invariants it is about to attack. Every perturbation harness implements five phases in order: establish_baseline, perturb, assert_perturbation (non-vacuity and target-match), run_subject, assert_specific_diagnostic. POSITIVE gates — kernel, World, bridge — need no additional 'must report nothing' test, because they ARE baseline observations. What needs this invariant is any claim of the form 'I changed X and therefore X caused this failure', which is exactly what a negative case asserts. Between round 14 and round 17 the negative battery's baseline was red and no case was isolated-cause evidence; nothing was falsely green, and that is a different and weaker property than the one the roster was reporting. AND A GATE MUST BE ABLE TO FAIL. A runner that pipes its subject into another command takes the exit status of the PIPE, not of the subject, so a gate whose subject CRASHED prints a stack trace's last line and reports success. Every governance recipe therefore captures its subject's output and status before printing, and the failure is verified in both directions: an unresolvable import and a failing assertion must each fail the target.
entries.evidence: negative_battery.sh: establish_baseline() runs grid_check on the unperturbed fixture and refuses the whole run if it does not exit 0, printing that no case below is isolated-cause evidence. The baseline is established once because every case builds its fixture by the same recipe from the same source — and that is VERIFIED rather than assumed: each case compares its own pre-perturbation digest against the baselined tree and fails FIXTURE DRIFT otherwise. harness_selftest.sh M-9 keeps the species in the bounded nine. Paired probes satisfy the convention by construction, since their live half IS the baseline and must be confined for the probe to pass. DECLARED OPEN: the one-directional 9D probes (maintainer, coordinator_alias, realm, ownfailopen, closureenv) assert a breach without first asserting that the honest fixture holds the invariants they attack; their baselines are not yet established in code. The runner half is EXECUTABLE as runner_contract.sh, 3/3: a throwaway make target built from the governance recipe form itself must succeed on a subject that exits 0, and fail on a subject that exits 1 and on a subject that crashes without printing. Deliberately NOT a tenth harness species — the nine are about falsifier non-vacuity, and process-status propagation is a different layer: whether the runner can hear the subject at all.

entries.statement: An ownership boundary that cannot own an object must REFUSE the object, never return the caller's reference. v0.10.0 ended in `catch { return v }`, so anything neither canonicalBytes nor structuredClone could handle was handed straight back with the authority the layer existed to take. Ownership now goes through canonicalBytes alone and throws <field>-not-canonical on failure, for spec.inputs, warrant.value and warrant.witness alike. A witness may be semantically OPAQUE without being representationally ARBITRARY: if it participates in warrant_id it needs a canonical representation. Should tagged encodings for Map/Set/Date ever be required, one encoding must serve ownership, equality, warrant_id and replay together.
entries.evidence: probe_ownfailopen_9d3_repro.mjs, 0/3 confined against World 0.10.0 and 3/3 against 0.11.0 with named refusals. A witness carrying a method defeated both mechanisms and came back by reference; a Map witness passed structuredClone while Object.freeze left its ENTRIES writable — and since JSON.stringify(Map) is '{}', Map([['e',1]]) and Map([['e',999]]) were indistinguishable to warrant identity, so the ownership domain and the identity domain disagreed about what a value is; and spec.inputs took the whole registration-alias species back, with B re-deriving on a caller-mutated input mid-pass.

entries.statement: A derivation's authority must be bounded by what the coordinator can own. Under the current same-realm arbitrary-closure measureFn API it is NOT, and this law is FALSIFIED BY DESIGN rather than repaired: capturing an arbitrary callable does not capture its semantics, and a function reference may retain mutable authority that is neither enumerable nor ownable. The witness needs no mutable object at all — a `let bias = 0` shared by two closures. Object.freeze, deepFreeze, structuredClone, canonicalBytes, #private fields, GuardedStore and the pass-entry snapshot are all INAPPLICABLE, because JavaScript provides no mechanism to enumerate, copy, canonicalize or freeze a captured lexical environment; freezing measureFn itself does not help either. A second theorem fails with it: derivation_id is computed from measure/predicate/inputs and therefore does NOT identify a derivation's semantics — the witness holds derivation_id constant while behaviour changes from fb to fb+1000. Tolerable as an acknowledged limit of the closure API; NOT tolerable once semantic films assert that an identified program performed a particular transition. Closure is by REPLACING the API, not by hardening it: see realm_roadmap.
entries.evidence: probe_closureenv_repro.mjs against World 0.11.0 — B is support_changed and re-derives to 1005 where an honest B is 5, in both the coordinator and the World, with derivation_id unchanged and the pass not aborted. Frozen and deliberately NOT gated: the probe exits 0 because it documents a boundary rather than a regression. Four ownership rounds (9D.1 raw maps and caller objects, 9D.2 nested values, 9D.3 fail-open ownership, and this) converged on the conclusion that an arbitrary closure is an unbounded capability container — an architectural boundary, not a missing Object.freeze.

entries.statement: A derivation crosses an authority boundary as DATA or not at all. The program is a canonical AST and program_sem_id is H(canonical program), so it cannot be a caller-selected label and cannot be rebound — the id IS the program's hash, and the same program has the same id under every conforming implementation while implementation_id carries executable provenance separately. The message domain is TRVM's canonical value domain, never 'structuredClone succeeded': Function, Map, Set, Date, class instances and transferable handles are refused, because those are capabilities rather than data. Reads are an AUTHORITY operation performed on the authoritative side and passed as explicit grants, so the derivation realm holds no world reference and needs none. A result produced on the far side is a CLAIM; it becomes evidence only when the authority re-derives it and the canonical bytes agree.
entries.evidence: derive_battery.mjs 10/10 in-process and derive_realm_battery.mjs 5/5 across a real worker_threads boundary. The decisive one is empirical: posting a request carrying a closure throws DataCloneError, so the 9D.4 lexical-cell attack — which no Object.freeze, deepFreeze, canonicalBytes, #private field or GuardedStore could reach — has NO TRANSPORT. The confinement is performed by the boundary rather than by object discipline, which is why replacing the API was the right response to law:derivation.environment-confinement@1 rather than hardening it further. SCOPE, stated rather than implied: this closes derivation-object-confinement only. Determinism of a long-lived evaluator (a worker holding `let counter = 0` leaks no parent authority and still fails to make program_sem_id denote a stable function) and host confinement (Date.now, Math.random, filesystem, network) are separate scopes, unclaimed here.
entries.revision_note: kept as history, and it is the honest record of an overclaim. Two sentences of this statement were not supported by the mechanism: 'reads are an AUTHORITY operation performed on the authoritative side and passed as explicit grants' described a worker that actually sourced its read table from canonical_inputs, where {op:'input', name:'__reads'} retrieved the whole table with zero tracked reads; and implementation_id was a caller-asserted field that no executor verified and no result carried. Both reproduced (probe_derivegrant_v02_repro.mjs, W-1 and W-2). Revision 2 states what the v0.2.0 mechanism does.

entries.statement: A derivation crosses an authority boundary as DATA or not at all. The program is a canonical AST and program_sem_id is H(canonical program), so it cannot be a caller-selected label and cannot be rebound — the id IS the program's hash, and the same program has the same id under every conforming implementation. The derivation realm holds no world reference and reads ONLY the grant snapshot the authority resolved for it, addressed through read/scope — never through input, which addresses canonical_inputs alone. A result produced on the far side is a CLAIM; it becomes evidence only when the authority validates its footprint against the grant it issued and re-derives the SEMANTIC PROJECTION of the result — every field but implementation_id — to the same canonical bytes.

Determinism of a long-lived evaluator and host confinement (Date.now, Math.random, filesystem, network) are separate scopes, unclaimed here.
entries.revision_note: kept as history. @2 said program_sem_id 'cannot be a caller-selected label' and that 'the same program has the same id under every conforming implementation' — both true of the SYNTAX and neither established for the SEMANTICS, because the id was H('TRVM-PROGRAM-v1|' + canonical AST) over an unfrozen language. Four behaviours could differ behind one id and all four were reproduced: add was JavaScript '+', bind() validated nothing, arity and field sets were unconstrained, and evaluation order was free while the footprint was an ordered sequence inside the semantic projection. Frozen as C-1..C-4 in probe_coresem_v03_repro.mjs.

entries.statement: A derivation crosses an authority boundary as DATA or not at all, and its identity commits the SEMANTICS of the language it is written in. program_sem_id = H('TRVM-PROGRAM-v2' | core_sem_id | canonical AST), where core_sem_id = H(canonical TRVM-DERIVE-CORE specification) — so a caller cannot select an id, an id cannot be rebound, AND an implementation cannot assign different meaning to an operation while agreeing on the id: a different core is a different program. The grammar is validated BEFORE an id is issued, so no identity exists for a program outside the language. The message domain is TRVM's canonical value domain, never 'structuredClone succeeded'. The derivation realm holds no world reference and reads ONLY its grant snapshot, addressed through read/scope and never through input. A result produced on the far side is a CLAIM; it becomes evidence only when the authority validates its footprint against the grant it issued and re-derives the semantic projection — every field but implementation_id and read_trace — to the same canonical bytes.

The decisive confinement result is still empirical: posting a request carrying a closure throws DataCloneError, so the 9D.4 lexical-cell attack has NO TRANSPORT. SCOPE: object confinement only. Determinism of a long-lived evaluator and host confinement are separate scopes, unclaimed here.

entries.statement: TRVM-DERIVE-CORE-v1 is FROZEN and its identity is content-bound. The record declares the grammar (every node's key set is exactly {op} union the op's declared fields), the value domain, arithmetic (IEEE-754 binary64, no coercion — operands must be numbers and results must be finite, overflow refused AT the operation), the identification of -0 with +0 in the canonical numeric quotient, evaluation order (depth-first, `a` before `b`, DETERMINISTIC so that refusals and traces reproduce but deliberately NOT semantic identity), read_footprint as a canonical DEPENDENCY SET with access order preserved separately in read_trace outside the semantic projection, totality (no recursion, no loop, no general function), and the exact refusal vocabulary. core_sem_id = H(canonical CORE_SPEC) rather than the label 'TRVM-DERIVE-CORE-v1', because a bare name is precisely the caller-selected identity the primitive ruling already refuses for 'componentReachability'. Changing what add means moves core_sem_id and therefore every program_sem_id, which is the property that makes the identity semantic rather than syntactic. A prim extension bumps the core version and every program id with it: a program written against a different language is a different program.
entries.evidence: probe_coresem_v03_repro.mjs — C-1 (add was JavaScript '+'), C-2 ({op:'exec', cmd:'rm -rf /'} was issued an id), C-3 (const-without-value, add-without-b and add-with-an-extra-field all issued ids), C-4 (the footprint was an ordered sequence, so a right-to-left implementation returned different canonical bytes for a program it computed identically) — 4/4 reproduce against the frozen v0.2.0 copy, 5/5 confined live. derive_battery.mjs: core-id-is-content-bound, program-id-commits-the-core, grammar-refuses-before-id (6 malformed programs), arithmetic-typed-and-total, footprint-is-a-canonical-set, trace-is-outside-the-semantic-projection, footprint-set-is-checked-not-normalized, overflow-refused-on-every-operator, coercion-refused-on-every-operator, signed-zero-identified. BREAKING BY DESIGN: every v0.2.0 program id is retired, done now precisely because no second implementation exists to be broken by it.

entries.statement: NON-SEMANTIC DOES NOT MEAN UNVERIFIED. A DeriveResult carries two explicit envelopes with different trust rules. semantic_result (value, witness, support, read_footprint) determines portable meaning and is what cross-implementation validation compares. execution_evidence (implementation_id, read_trace) carries conformance and provenance: it is EXCLUDED from that comparison and NOT excluded from checking. The core fixes evaluation order — depth-first, `a` before `b` — precisely so that refusals and traces reproduce, so a returned trace that disagrees with the authority's own re-derivation is a CONFORMANCE failure of the implementation rather than a disagreement about the program, and it is refused as trace-nonconforming. The two verdicts are reported SEPARATELY — semantic_agreement and trace_conforms — because 'same meaning, different strategy' and 'wrong answer' are different diagnoses. The flat shape was part of the defect: a field sitting beside value and read_footprint reads as authenticated by the same machinery as its neighbours. Later the semantic film supersedes the trace check and lives in this same envelope.
entries.evidence: probe_traceforge_v06_repro.mjs — T-1: a program reading a then b, with ONLY the trace reversed and the canonical footprint and value untouched, passed validateForeignResult and was accepted with validated + fresh_at_check under v0.5.0. checkResult compared the footprint to the SET of the trace, which a reversal does not change, and the semantic projection excluded the trace — so the one field carrying execution evidence was the one field nothing looked at. 1/1 reproduces against the frozen v0.5.0 validation and 4/4 confined live. derive_battery.mjs: trace-is-outside-the-semantic-projection, plus the envelope schema checks in checkResult.

entries.statement: Containment and freshness are different questions and a protocol needs both. footprintWithinGrant asks a HISTORICAL question — was every claimed read inside the snapshot this derivation received? validateFootprintFresh asks a TEMPORAL one — are those dependencies still current at the moment of acceptance? Both can be satisfied about a World that has moved, so re-derivation against the grant can never detect staleness: executor and authority agree perfectly about an old snapshot. Freshness keys on the FOOTPRINT and never on a global vclock — an unrelated write must not invalidate a derivation that did not depend on it, or the grant/footprint separation is undone from the other side. Exact reads compare versions; scope predicates compare digests, which is the World's phantom-scope case reaching the derivation boundary. ACCEPTANCE DOES NOT ESTABLISH COMMITTABILITY. One call cannot: the World can move between it returning and the caller applying. It establishes `validated` and `fresh_at_check` — an observation at a moment — and the composition that commits belongs to the World: acquire the authoritative lock, accept, deterministic prepared apply with no hostile callback in between, seal the receipt, release. No lock capability is exported to reach that, because rounds 9B-9C are the record of what happens when transaction authority gets passed around.
entries.evidence: probe_stalegrant_v03_repro.mjs: grant cut at fb@1=5, derived, World moved to fb@2=9 — checkResult PASS, footprintWithinGrant PASS, validateForeignResult PASS, all three CORRECT, and acceptance refuses 'stale-read: fb granted@1 live@2'. Plus the negative half (unrelated-write-ignored) and the scope half (stale-scope: kind:node, a node joining a query with no exact read moving). derive_battery.mjs: freshness-is-not-containment, unrelated-write-does-not-invalidate, acceptance-does-not-claim-committable. derive_realm_battery.mjs: intent-to-acceptance across a real worker.

entries.statement: An authority-issued request authenticates THE WHOLE REQUEST, and acceptance takes no proof from its caller. grant_id is a hash of the grant and a hash authenticates content to itself, so it proves integrity and says nothing about issuance; binding request_id to grant_id answers 'was this issued?' about a GRANT while the thing being accepted is a REQUEST. Issuance therefore records request_id -> request_sem_id = H(canonical request), recomputed at acceptance, so any change to any field is a different request rather than the same request with different content. The authority is the only constructor of a DeriveRequest; a caller submits a DeriveIntent and may REQUEST exactly one thing, expected_implementation_id, which is a requirement on the executor rather than authority content — an open options bag spread after the authority's own fields is a caller writing authority content. Acceptance is a METHOD on the authority, closing over its issuance table and its live World reader: a free function taking those as parameters, with the issuer defaulting to absent, lets the caller supply both proofs of its own authority. The issued request is owned through canonicalBytes and deep-frozen as defence in depth, not as the boundary — the binding is the boundary. A signature or MAC is added when, and only when, the grant crosses a real trust boundary, is persisted and replayed later, is delegated between authorities, or must be proved to an independent verifier.
entries.evidence: probe_issuebind_v05_repro.mjs, 3/3 reproduced against the frozen draft and 4/4 confined live. I-1: swapping canonical_inputs under an untouched request_id and grant_id passed wasIssued, derived 1005 where an honest request derives 5, and was accepted as committable. I-2: authorize(intent, {canonical_inputs:{bias:1000}}) produced an AUTHORITY-ISSUED request evaluating to 1005. I-3: acceptance with the issuer argument OMITTED accepted a wholly self-made request, and a fake liveReader replaying the granted version turned a stale-read refusal back into an acceptance. derive_battery.mjs: issuance-binds-the-whole-request, request-sem-id-recomputes, authorize-options-whitelisted, issued-request-is-owned-and-frozen, intent-schema-closed, authority-requires-a-world.

entries.statement: The authority grant and the read footprint are TWO evidence objects and may not be collapsed into one. The grant (read_grants, named by grant_id = H(canonical read_grants)) is a CAPABILITY record: what the authority made available, resolved on the authoritative side, deliberately permitted to be broader than what is read because under data-dependent traversal the needed subset is not knowable in advance. The footprint is the DEPENDENCY record: what the program actually consumed through a tracked read or scope, recorded by the evaluator on access. Freshness, invalidation, replay and support analysis key on the footprint alone — defining it as the grant would over-invalidate every derivation whose grant was wider than its reads, which under snapshot granting is all of them. The authority validates the footprint as a SUBSET of the grant, at the granted versions and scope digests, on its own evidence and BEFORE any re-derivation.
entries.evidence: derive_battery.mjs: grant-not-reachable-as-input, footprint-is-the-access-subset (a 3-resource grant against a 1-entry footprint), grant-id-binds-the-snapshot (a swapped snapshot under the original grant_id is refused request-grant-id-mismatch), footprint-validated-independently (footprint-ungranted-read / footprint-version-mismatch, both fired on an otherwise honest result), witness-matches-footprint. derive_realm_battery.mjs repeats the input-reachability and forged-footprint cases across a real worker. The v0.1.0 defect is frozen as W-1 in probe_derivegrant_v02_repro.mjs and must keep reproducing there. GRANTING MODEL, decided rather than defaulted: snapshot (A) not read-RPC (B) — deterministic, films cleanly, no cross-realm round trip per primitive. Its cost is least-authority, since the grant may reveal more than the program reads; confidentiality against the derivation realm is the stated trigger to revisit.

entries.statement: Execution identity is ASSERTED BY THE EXECUTOR and may only be REQUIRED by the caller. DeriveResult carries implementation_id, emitted by the evaluator that ran; DeriveRequest carries at most expected_implementation_id, which an executor that cannot satisfy it refuses by name. A caller therefore cannot cause a result to claim an implementation that did not produce it. The field is excluded from the semantic projection that cross-implementation validation compares, which is what lets a C result and a JS result of the same program_sem_id agree while their provenance stays distinguishable — the film_identity_forward_declaration split, made operative. DECLARED OPEN: implementation_id is a declared constant, not a digest of executable bytes, so this closes IMPERSONATION and does not yet establish PROVENANCE — a modified JS worker still emits impl-js-derive-v0.2.0. Binding it to a source/binary digest is the next revision and is named here rather than implied.
entries.evidence: derive_battery.mjs: implementation-id-asserted, implementation-requirement-refused, implementation-id-well-formed, semantic-projection-is-portable (a result stamped impl-c-derive-v0.2.0 validates and its provenance is reported rather than compared away), implementation-requirement-checked-on-result. derive_realm_battery.mjs: executor-asserts-implementation across the worker boundary, and cross-implementation-shape — which is the SHAPE a real C implementation plugs into and explicitly not a claim that one exists. The v0.1.0 defect is frozen as W-2: a request asserting impl-c-pretend-v9 was executed by the JS evaluator and returned success, with no implementation_id in the result at all.
entries.revision_note: KEPT AS THE RECORD OF A FALSE CLAIM, shipped for seven rounds. @1 said 'A caller therefore cannot cause a result to claim an implementation that did not produce it' and 'this closes IMPERSONATION and does not yet establish PROVENANCE'. The first half was false. deriveLocally took the implementation identity as a PARAMETER, so a caller could run the JS evaluator and stamp its honest output 'impl-c-derive-…', after which acceptance compared the caller's expectation against the caller's own label — a claim against a claim — and returned ok with trace_conforms:true, which made the forgery read as better attested than an unforged result. Reproduced as P-1 in probe_execclaim_v07_repro.mjs. The declared-open item was also mis-scoped: hashing the executable would NOT have closed it, because a digest carried inside the same untrusted result is still self-asserted.

entries.statement: AN EXECUTION CLAIM IS NOT PROVENANCE. A canonical result arriving from outside is an untrusted execution CLAIM however perfect its bytes are, and no property of the result can establish which executor produced it — not a conforming trace, not a version string, and not a digest of the executable, because a digest carried inside the same untrusted result is self-asserted too. The only thing here that is not a claim is what the HOST OBSERVED IT LAUNCH. So: an implementation's identity comes from the implementation and never from a caller-supplied parameter; validateForeignResult establishes semantic agreement and trace conformance and explicitly NOT provenance, reporting implementation_claimed rather than certifying it; the authority records what it launched via an authority-issued executor handle; and acceptance compares the request's expected_implementation_id against the OBSERVATION, refuses implementation-claim-contradicts-observation when the result's label disagrees with it, and answers implementation-provenance-unavailable — never 'verified' — where no observation exists. Three distinct objects, and round 19's two envelopes were one short: semantic_result is portable MEANING, execution_evidence is the execution CLAIM, and the host's observation is the only OBSERVATION. DECLARED OPEN, now correctly scoped: WHAT identity a native executable should register — a trusted launcher hashing the binary it is about to exec — is unbuilt. WHETHER an independent observation exists at all is no longer optional.
entries.evidence: probe_execclaim_v07_repro.mjs: P-1 reproduces against the frozen v0.6.0 acceptance (JS produces every byte, the caller chooses the label, accept returns ok with implementation_id impl-c-derive-v0.6.0 and trace_conforms true) and 6/6 confined live — the caller cannot select a label at all; provenance is 'observed' only with a host handle and 'unavailable' without one, with NO implementation_id reported in that case; a C claim against an observed JS executor is refused; a C requirement with no observation is refused as unavailable; and an executor handle carries a private Symbol the authority minted so it cannot be fabricated. derive_battery.mjs: provenance-requires-observation, claim-checked-against-observation, executor-handles-are-authority-issued, registered-identity-well-formed, validator-does-not-do-provenance, acceptance-success-shape-narrow. trace_conforms is removed from the acceptance success shape — redundant there, and a boolean per check invites weighing them — while staying in the validator and in the failure diagnostics where semantic_agreement:true + trace_conforms:false is the distinction worth having.
entries.revision_note: SUPERSEDED, and kept as the record of a mechanism that did not do what its own statement said. @2 opened 'AN EXECUTION CLAIM IS NOT PROVENANCE' — which is right and survives into @3 — and then named as its mechanism 'the authority records what it launched via an authority-issued executor handle'. It launched nothing. registerExecutor(implementation_id) took a STRING, put it in a private Map, and returned a handle carrying a private Symbol; the Symbol proved that this authority minted this handle and nothing about any execution. So P-1 did not close, it MOVED: v0.6 let the caller choose the identity at deriveLocally(), v0.7 let it choose the identity at registerExecutor(). And accept(registry, req, res, executor = null) put a proof back in the caller's hands — the exact shape round 17 removed from issuance, one level up — so even a registration that really launched C could have had its handle paired with bytes produced elsewhere. Frozen as P-2 and P-2b in probe_execreg_v08_repro.mjs, which reproduces both against a verbatim frozen copy.

entries.statement: EXECUTOR EXISTENCE IS NOT EXECUTION PROVENANCE. Proving that an executor exists — even proving which bytes it is made of — says nothing about which bytes came back from which request. An observation must bind the EXECUTOR, the REQUEST and the RETURNED BYTES as one execution event, and acceptance must take no part of that proof from its caller. This is round 17's issuance lesson one level higher: there, don't authenticate the grant, authenticate the WHOLE REQUEST; here, don't authenticate the executor handle, authenticate the WHOLE EXECUTION EVENT. So: manual registration is DELETED; the authority is the thing that runs an executor (execute(req, launcher)); a launcher supplies MECHANISM AND NO IDENTITY — where the artifact's files are and how to start them — and the authority reads and hashes those files itself, resolves the family name from its own digest→name POLICY, spawns, sends that request, takes those bytes, and only then records an observation keyed by H(request_sem_id | canonical(the whole result)); and accept(registry, req, res) consults that privately held table, so a relabelled result MISSES the observation rather than being compared against it. THREE IDENTITIES, because one string was answering three questions: implementation_family_id (what implementation this is), executable_artifact_id (H of the bytes the authority read), and executor_session_id (this particular authority-driven launch). The naming policy is not an observation — it says what bytes are CALLED, never that anything ran — and it is injective in both directions so a caller cannot rewrite it mid-run. DECLARED OPEN, stated conservatively on purpose: hashing a path and then spawning that path supports 'the host observed artifact X immediately before requesting execution of path P'. It is NOT a proof that the OS executed those exact bytes under every filesystem race, and it is not hardware-attested executable identity. Also uncovered: the node binary and standard library for a JS executor, and every shared object the loader binds for a native one.

entries.revision_note: SUPERSEDED, and it was right about the half it named. @3 said the authority must read and hash the artifact ITSELF rather than believe a name, and that stands. What it did not say is that hashing the declaration establishes nothing about what was then invoked. v0.8.0's launcher carried `artifact_files` (the evidence, honestly hashed) beside `spawn` (an independent caller-controlled action), two fields of one object with nothing binding them — so declaring the genuine JS worker closure, naming that digest as C, and supplying a spawn() that evaluated in-process returned implementation_provenance 'observed' for impl-c-derive with no C anywhere. The same shape held in the film plane against the real C binary's genuine digest. What actually held was 'authority read bytes X, then invoked callback Y'. Frozen as P-3 and P-3F in probe_execlaunch_v09_repro.mjs.

entries.statement: ARTIFACT OBSERVATION DOES NOT ESTABLISH EXECUTION PROVENANCE UNLESS THE MECHANISM INVOKED IS MECHANICALLY DERIVED FROM THE ARTIFACT OBSERVED. Equivalently, and this is the operative form: a launch descriptor may not carry both the evidence and an independent executable action. @1 let the caller pick the label, @2 let it pick the name a registration would report, @3 made the authority hash real bytes and then call a function the caller had supplied beside them. Each revision closed one supplier and left the next; the pattern is that any field a caller controls on the launch path becomes the provenance. So the caller supplies NOTHING on that path. ObservedExecutionHost is constructed with an IMMUTABLE EXECUTOR CATALOG — family name to {kind, entrypoint, artifact_closure}, deep-frozen, injective, refusing an entrypoint outside its own hashed closure and refusing any entry field beyond those three. The transport for each kind is written in the host. execute(registry, req) names a family and nothing else; the invocation is DATA and is canonicalised, which refuses a function outright. Both authorities — derivation and film — share this host and share no semantics with it: it cannot re-derive a result, replay a film, or say what either means. Duplicating the semantic boundary is the fence; duplicating the mechanism reproduced the defect in both planes, which is how it was found twice. Acceptance reports executor_sessionS, plural. The key is over BYTES, so two launches producing byte-identical output share it; reporting a single session id claims a uniqueness the key cannot support, and @3's implementation overwrote the earlier record besides. DECLARED OPEN, unchanged: hash-then-launch supports 'the host observed artifact X immediately before requesting execution of path P'. It is NOT a proof that the OS executed those exact bytes under every filesystem race, and it is not hardware-attested executable identity. The node binary, its flags and the standard library are uncovered for a JS entry; every shared object the loader binds is uncovered for a native one.

entries.statement: THE EXECUTION PLANE ORIGINATES EVIDENCE, RATHER THAN THE GOVERNANCE PLANE RECONSTRUCTING IT AROUND THE EXECUTION PLANE AFTERWARDS. For a frozen one-step fixture, the native C runtime independently emits a semantic-film frame whose pre-state, enabled rule, canonical locus, post-state and terminal status are accepted by the existing TRVM-SEMFILM-v1.1 contract WITHOUT normalization or translation of meaning — the law kernel's own replaySemFilm, imported unmodified, replaying on a fresh runtime. Every field is derived by the emitter from its own execution: the redex is found by an enumeration that mirrors findAppRedexes over ic32's packed-word heap, the rule is the rule that fired, quiescence is the same enumeration run again and required to be empty, and the readback is required to be PURE (resolving the state must cost no interaction). SCOPE, checked rather than assumed: MULTI-FRAME films over APP-plane rules, on terms that may CARRY dup cells, C→JS only. v0.1.0 scoped itself by dup PRESENCE and that was the right refusal for the wrong reason — the lowered add(const 2, const 3) carries dup cells and, under the leftmost-tree-app strategy, fires none, so the blocker was ENABLEDNESS all along. A term where a DUP-* rule becomes enabled is REFUSED BY NAME (film-dup-rule-enabled); so is a term already in normal form; and the terminal re-checks pool-quiescence rather than inheriting it from the loop. STILL UNBUILT and named: the six DUP-* rules, the d: and v: loci, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED terminals. AND ONE CHECK WAS REMOVED BECAUSE IT WAS ACCIDENTALLY TRUE. v0.1.0 asserted the readback fired ZERO interactions; on a one-step dup-free fixture resolving the state costs nothing, so a machine counter that never moved looked like a verified property. ic32's `interactions` is not plane-classified, so comparing it against zero measures a different quantity from the kernel's INTERACT-plane claim — it fires four on the lowered term whose state is nonetheless correct. The count is now REPORTED and pool-quiescence is what is ASSERTED. The C-side checker — films flowing the other direction — is not claimed. A film arriving from outside is an execution CLAIM exactly as a DeriveResult is, so film provenance uses the same discipline as derivation.implementation-provenance@4: the shared ObservedExecutionHost, an immutable catalog entry naming the binary, hash-then-launch, and an observation keyed over the whole emission rather than over the film alone — provenance is over everything the executor emitted, not over a subset a caller chose to present. REPLAY AND PROVENANCE ARE REPORTED SEPARATELY, because a film can be semantically perfect and its claimed provenance false; P-3F is exactly that case. THE TWO TRANSITION SYSTEMS STAY SEPARATE (film_planes): the TRVM calculus film is pre-state → (rule + locus) → post-state over the ic32 interaction-net relation, and the derivation evidence relation is DeriveRequest → evaluate → DeriveResult. What is shared is HOST INFRASTRUCTURE, not semantics.

The frame's endpoints are the corpus vector's own initial and normal_form states, which the 48/48 bridge gate had already shown C and JS agree on byte-for-byte, so the new claim is exactly the TRANSITION between two states whose canonicalization was never in doubt. Seven forgeries, each RE-COMMITTED (frame_id and film_id recomputed) so it dies on a semantic check rather than on bookkeeping: F-1 wrong pre-state (sem-revision-mismatch), F-2 wrong post-state (sem-post-mismatch), F-3 a real rule at a wrong locus (sem-locus-not-enabled), F-4 a real redex misdescribed as a dup rule (sem-rule-mismatch), F-5 the honest film replayed against another source term (sem-revision-mismatch), F-6 a genuine C observation that cannot be re-pointed at another film, and F-7 an edit to the frame's DECLARED-NON-AUTHORITATIVE index i, which still REPLAYS and still loses provenance — replay and provenance being different verdicts. ic32_film.c #includes ic32_canon.c under IC32_CANON_NO_MAIN, so the canonicalizer beneath the film is the same code the bridge gate replays rather than a copy written for the occasion; the bridge stays 48/48 after the guard. entries.statement: AN AUTHORITY CANNOT VALIDATE A SEMANTIC CLAIM USING A PROGRAM RESOLVER SUPPLIED BY THE CLAIMANT. Acceptance takes no proof from its caller — INCLUDING the mapping from semantic identity to semantic program. Re-derivation is only evidence if the authority chose what it re-derived against. The supplier ladder this closes has four rungs and one shape: @1 the caller supplied the implementation LABEL (deriveLocally's third parameter), @2 the registration NAME (registerExecutor), @3 the ACTION beside the artifact evidence (a launcher's spawn), @4 the SEMANTIC ORACLE at acceptance (accept's registry parameter). Any field a caller controls on the path to a verdict becomes the verdict. AN instanceof CHECK DOES NOT CLOSE IT, and a law that read as 'check the type' would invite exactly the wrong repair: a Proxy satisfies the type, and so does a genuine ProgramRegistry the caller populated with a different program. The repair is OWNERSHIP. The registry is BUILT at the authority's construction from canonical program DATA — ProgramRegistry.bind severs it through canonicalBytes — so the authority owns its semantic oracle rather than sharing an object with whoever built it, and no registry parameter crosses execute() or accept() again. bindProgram remains an explicit authority operation and needs no second rule, because ids are content-bound: teaching the authority const(999) gives it a new id and cannot repoint const(5)'s. So every oracle the authority consults is constructor-time — the World reader (round 17), the semantic registry (here), and the execution host with its immutable catalog (derivation.implementation-provenance@4) — and what a caller supplies is an INTENT and a RESULT TO VALIDATE.

entries.statement: ONE SOURCE PROGRAM UNDER ONE LOWERING SEMANTICS DETERMINES ONE CANONICAL TARGET TERM. lowering_sem_id identifies the lowering SEMANTICS — H over the source core_sem_id, the target term encoding id, the canonical lowering specification and the conformance-vector identity — and is a different object from a record of what happened when a particular program was lowered, which is a LoweringReceipt {program_sem_id, lowering_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}. One id must not silently answer both 'which lowering semantics is this?' and 'what did lowering do here?'. THE INSTRUMENT IS RE-LOWERING, NOT A FILM. A semantic film is evidence for a TRANSITION SYSTEM; lowering is a relation DeriveProgram -> TargetTerm. Filming it would invent a sequence of internal compiler steps and make implementation strategy semantic — the mistake the read-order ruling refused when it kept access order out of the footprint. Verification is: re-lower the program independently under lowering_sem_id, canonicalise, and require target_term_sem_id to agree. DEFERRED AND NAMED: whether lowering is PARAMETERIZED (program -> target term with input ports, inputs arriving at execution, so target_term_sem_id is a function of the program alone) or INSTANTIATED (program + canonical_inputs -> closed target term, in which case the identity must say so). The first witness uses inputs={} and does not decide it. That decision comes BEFORE the input op, because an unstated variable inside target_term_sem_id is the hidden-identity bug class round 16 exists to prevent.
entries.evidence: lowering_check.mjs: lowering-is-deterministic (the same AST lowers to the same string twice, and the RELATION id is separate from the APPLICATION receipt), re-lowering-verifies (lowering again independently reaches the same target_term_sem_id, and add(3,2) reaches a different one so the id is not vacuous), out-of-fragment-refused (input, read, sub, a non-integer constant and a negative constant are each a NAMED refusal). native-execution-observed cross-checks the target term's identity against the C side: the kernel's target_term_sem_id equals ic32_canon's canonical id for the same lowered term, so both planes agree on what was fed in before either says what came out.

entries.statement: ONE CANONICAL TARGET NORMAL FORM UNDER ONE DECODER DETERMINES ONE STRUCTURAL TRVM OUTCOME, OR A STRUCTURAL DECODE REFUSAL. decode_sem_id identifies the decoder, and decoding is a THIRD relation rather than the tail of lowering: a lowering can be perfect while the decoder reads the normal form wrongly, and a decoder can be perfect while lowering emitted the wrong target term. They fail independently, so they are proved independently. The outcome is STRUCTURAL — {status:'value', value} or {status:'refused', code, locus} — never a rendered reason, which would recreate round 16's 'the identity bound a spelling' one layer up. The decoder reads the CANONICAL SIGNATURE rather than a readback string — the same bytes the 48/48 bridge has agreed on since round 12 — so it cannot be misled by a binder name. §5 compaction is irreversible, so a compacted signature is REFUSED rather than guessed at; that bounds the decodable numerals and the bound is stated rather than discovered.
entries.evidence: lowering_check.mjs: decode-is-structural (L0(L1(A(N0,…A(N0,N1)…))) with five applications decodes to {status:'value', value:5}) and decoder-boundary-named (a non-numeral is decode-not-a-church-numeral, a compacted signature is decode-signature-compacted, and 0 and 1 decode — the two shapes that carry no dup). decode_sem_id is distinct from lowering_sem_id and asserted so.

entries.statement: SOURCE AND TARGET AGREE ON THE OUTCOME: source_outcome_sem_id == target_outcome_sem_id, where the target side is reached by canonical lowering, native ic32 execution, and structural decoding. TWO GRADES OF EVIDENCE FOR THE EXECUTION LEG, and only the first is claimed here. OBSERVED: the ObservedExecutionHost hashed a catalogued binary and then ran it, so the normal form is an execution event the host drove (derivation.implementation-provenance@4). FILM-EVIDENCED: the transition sequence itself is replayed by the independent kernel (film.native-emission@1). BOTH ARE NOW CLAIMED for the first witness: ic32_film v0.2.0 emits six chained APP-LAM frames for the lowered term and the kernel replays the chain. Round 25 recorded the second as OPEN on the strength of a refusal that was right about the fixture and wrong about its reason — the lowered term carries dup cells and fires none. What remains OPEN is a fixture where a DUP-* rule actually becomes enabled. Reporting the two grades separately is the point: an execution the host observed and an execution the kernel replayed are different claims. THIS IS THE THEOREM; canonical-lowering@1 and target-decoding@1 exist to make it DIAGNOSABLE, because a bare equality failure cannot say which of three relations broke. Six identities stay distinct and none may be collapsed into another: program_sem_id, lowering_sem_id, target_term_sem_id, target_nf_sem_id, decode_sem_id, outcome_sem_id. Collapsing any pair turns a refinement statement into a renaming, which is the failure mode this whole chain is built to avoid.
entries.evidence: lowering_check.mjs 9/9, the first end-to-end witness: add(const 2, const 3) with inputs={} lowers to one canonical ic32 term whose identity the kernel and ic32_canon agree on; the host launches the catalogued binary and observes the canonical normal form L0(L1(A(N0,A(N0,A(N0,A(N0,A(N0,N1))))))); that decodes structurally to {status:'value', value:5}; and its outcome id EQUALS the source evaluator's, whose result was itself accepted by an authority owning every oracle it consulted (derivation.acceptance-authority@1). six-identities-stay-distinct asserts all six values differ. native-film-absent-by-refusal asserts the film emitter REFUSES this exact fixture with film-dup-cell-present — the gap is measured at the fixture the refinement runs on rather than described in the abstract.

entries.statement: AN AUTHORITY-BEARING OBJECT MAY NOT BE SUPPLIED TO THE AUTHORITY THAT WILL TRUST IT. An `instanceof` guard is satisfied by a subclass: two overridden methods — run() that never runs and observationOf() that answers whatever it likes — pass `host instanceof ObservedExecutionHost` while bypassing the catalog, the digest, hash-then-launch and the observation table, all of which remain perfectly correct and perfectly unconsulted. Acceptance then reports implementation_provenance 'observed' for an implementation that never ran. THE QUESTION IS NOT WHAT THE OBJECT IS DESCENDED FROM. THE QUESTION IS WHO BUILT IT. So the repair is not a tighter predicate — Object.getPrototypeOf(host) === ObservedExecutionHost.prototype excludes the subclass and admits a Proxy, and would be derivation.acceptance-authority@1's mistake with a longer expression. The authority takes an EXECUTOR CATALOG, which is data, and constructs the host itself against its module's own class binding, which no caller can substitute. Every authority with such a parameter does the same, because this is a property of the PARAMETER and not of any one class. This is the fifth rung of one ladder: @1 the implementation LABEL, @2 the registration NAME, @3 the ACTION beside the artifact evidence, @4 the SEMANTIC ORACLE at acceptance, @5 the EXECUTION-AUTHORITY OBJECT itself. Each rung sat in the parameter that had stopped being examined because it was 'obviously infrastructure'. What a caller supplies is an INTENT, a RESULT TO VALIDATE, and — at construction only — the DATA every oracle is built from.
